basis: Adenomatous polyposis directly involves the colon; colorectal malignancy is a minority complication and separate diagnosis.
Cryptophthalmos and cutaneous syndactyly each occur in 3/4; bladder aplasia and renal agenesis define major urinary involvement. Other organ defects individually occur in 1/4.
Melanocytic malignancy assigned to the usual cutaneous origin; the supplied definition specifies histology without establishing an ocular site.
Classical complement immunodeficiency. SLE in approximately 60% and recurrent respiratory infections are separately diagnosed diseases; their organ effects are not assigned here.
Immune deficiency defined by chronic Candida infection of skin, nails and mucosa, particularly oral mucosa.
Sensorineural deafness and brittle twisted hair with alopecia define the syndrome. Nonspecific eye abnormalities do not establish ocular damage; hypogonadism is occasional.
Osteocartilaginous nodules occupy and may obstruct the trachea and bronchi; their composition does not indicate locomotor skeletal disease.
Neurodevelopmental disability defines the syndrome; hearing impairment and structural heart defects/arrhythmias are frequent (30-79%). Renal disease is occasional.
Tumour originates in uterine corpus smooth muscle, a reproductive site outside the axes; visceral smooth muscle is not skeletal muscle.
Disordered sleep regulation and sleep stages constitute neurologic dysfunction; no other organ damage consistently applies across this umbrella.
Common lung, circulatory and kidney failure; coagulation dysfunction occurs in roughly 30-50%. Hepatic and neurologic failure omitted under the four-axis cap; combinations vary.
Menstrual abnormalities are reproductive; the umbrella does not establish an endocrine disorder or blood-cell disease.
Limb dysplasia and atrioventricular canal defects define the syndrome; nail dysplasia occurs in 3/5 and conical teeth/diastema in 1/3, supporting skin and dental involvement.
Skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and profound intellectual disability occur in 80-99%, hearing impairment in 30-79%. Redundant skin alone does not establish damage.
A dental spacing abnormality affecting maxillary central incisors; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Mandibular hypoplasia, deafness and lipodystrophic insulin resistance define disease; skin/subcutis atrophy occurs in 4/4. Hepatic steatosis (2/3) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Defective renal tubular magnesium reabsorption causes persistent hypomagnesemia. Vertigo and weakness each occur in 1/4 and do not establish additional organ damage.
Glomus tumour arises in the skin; perivascular cell origin alone does not establish cardiovascular organ disease.
Hereditary short stature with skeletal abnormalities; the supplied subtypes support a primary skeletal disorder.
An astrocytic central nervous system tumour; BRAF mutation does not establish another organ axis.
Meningioma occupies the lateral ventricle of the brain.
Parainfluenza type 1 infects respiratory epithelium, characteristically producing upper airway disease and croup.
Dorsal midbrain dysfunction causes vertical gaze palsy and pupillary abnormalities; these central ocular-motor signs do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Teratoma originates in the ovary as a reproductive organ; endocrine dysfunction is not part of its definition.
Progressive immune-mediated CNS demyelination; direct optic nerve involvement with visual dysfunction occurs in roughly half over the MS course. Neurogenic bladder is secondary.
